extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, authors, journal editors and peer reviewers involved in in vivo/animal research reporting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing manuscripts reporting in vivo (animal) experiments so that studies are reported with sufficient transparency and detail for readers and reviewers to assess reliability and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as part of the ARRIVE Essential 10. The Essential 10 are the basic minimum items that must be included in any manuscript describing animal research; without this information readers and reviewers cannot assess the reliability of the findings. The ARRIVE site indicates each item includes examples of good reporting drawn from the literature and should be consulted during planning to improve experimental design and bias minimisation. See the ARRIVE Explanation & Elaboration for full details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Sample size is one of the minimum items required for manuscripts; omission prevents assessment of reliability. Examples and extended guidance are provided on the ARRIVE site and Explanation & Elaboration article (PLOS Biology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Authors should report inclusion/exclusion criteria as part of the minimum reporting information. The website provides explanatory examples to guide reporting and planning to reduce bias and improve transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomisation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Randomisation methods and procedures must be reported as part of the basic minimum to allow assessment of bias. Examples of good reporting and explanatory notes are available in the ARRIVE Explanation & Elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding/Masking
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Reporting who was blinded, at what stage, and how is required for reliable assessment. The ARRIVE site includes examples and further explanation to help authors report blinding appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome measures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Authors should clearly define outcome measures in the manuscript as part of the minimum reporting standard. The ARRIVE Explanation & Elaboration provides examples and rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Full reporting of statistical methods used (analyses performed, software, assumptions, etc.) is required as minimum information. ARRIVE supplies examples and guidance to improve reporting of analysis and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental animals
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Information about the animals used (species/strain/sex/age/weight, provenance) is required in manuscripts; the ARRIVE site gives examples of good reporting and explanatory context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Detailed description of procedures (what was done, how, when, by whom) is required as part of the minimum reporting standard. ARRIVE provides examples to illustrate adequate reporting for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ARRIVE Essential 10 item. Clear presentation of results (including summary data, variability, effect sizes, and measures of uncertainty) is required as minimum reporting. The site includes examples and further explanation in the Explanation & Elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the Recommended set. These items complement the Essential 10 and add important context to the study; reporting items from both sets represents best practice. The ARRIVE site provides examples and guidance on what to include in abstracts to improve transparency and interpretability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Authors should provide scientific background and rationale; Recommended items add context and represent best practice. Examples of good reporting are included in the ARRIVE Explanation & Elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Explicit statement of objectives or hypotheses is recommended to contextualise the study. ARRIVE provides examples and explanatory text to guide reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical statement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Reporting ethical approval/oversight and welfare considerations is recommended; this adds important context beyond the Essential 10. Guidance and examples are given on the ARRIVE site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing and husbandry
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Details of housing and husbandry conditions are recommended for reporting to aid interpretation and reproducibility. Examples are provided in the Explanation & Elaboration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal care and monitoring
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Reporting how animals were cared for and monitored (including humane endpoints) is recommended; ARRIVE supplies examples and explanatory guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation/ scientific implications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Authors should discuss interpretation and scientific implications of results; this item complements the Essential 10 to give fuller context and promote accurate conclusions. See ARRIVE Explanation & Elaboration for examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability/ translation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Authors should address the generalisability and translational relevance of findings; reporting this context is considered best practice and examples are provided by ARRIVE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol registration
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Reporting whether protocols were pre-registered (and where) is recommended to increase transparency and reduce reporting bias. ARRIVE includes explanatory materials and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Authors are recommended to report how and where study data and materials can be accessed to support reproducibility and reuse. ARRIVE provides guidance and examples for data-sharing statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaration of interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended set item. Authors should declare competing interests and funding sources; this contextual information is recommended as part of best practice reporting. ARRIVE supplies examples and explanatory guidance.
